page.layout: One block of verse in roman and italic, full width, with a running head at the top. Below the last line, at the right, the catchword "Et". No margin notes.

p.i: Teque amens crusti concludit in orbe nefandi Quod rerum ignari, & miserum quod vulgus adoret!

Aspicis hæc, & ferre potes scelera ista nefasque? Iræ tum patiens potes hæc tolerare tot annos? Quin potius terras iterum Pater obrue terras Diluvio, & penitus nunc rerum elementa laborent; Corruat & fractus jam nunc compage soluta Orbis, jamque nihil, nedum chaos omnia fiant: Aut cadat horrendo mundi cinefacta fragore Crudelis Babylon, terræ communis Erynnis Contemptrixque tui, & tantorum causa malorum Invadens miseras Veri sub imagine gentes, Parca boni, scelerum atque alienæ prodiga vitæ. Jam Romam furor ille tuus, Romaéque tribunal Sacrilegum, furor ille tuus nunc sulphuris imbre Corripiat, qualem mare prodigiale Sodomes Infandæ spirat, dirique bitumínis ater Gurges, & atra palus flammis infamibus undans. Quo quondam fœcunda loco, diti ubere tellus Proventus dabat ingentes frugumque merique, Nunc tantum infamis lacus, illuviéque nefanda Heu, squallens regio, & misero terra horrida vultu.

Te dira, heu, Babylon nondum rapit ignea cæli Tempestas, nec adhuc tristes haurire tenebræ Et caligo nocens, terræque immanis hiatus? Non Erebi fratres, nondum te tartara pœnis Exercent scelerata, hominumque Deique flagellum? Te super Omnipotens ægrum nunquámne furore Terribilis pluet incumbens, penitúsque recidet?

Sed quid ego? non sic Deus omnia protinus igne Corripit, aut fontes lachrymoso protinus orco Plectit, sed justum expectat (ne accersite) tempus, Quô scelus in cumulum crescat, molisque nefandæ Incrementum ingens, ac jam se ferre laboret:

page.notes: Running head "PROTREPTICON" is in spaced capitals at the top centre. No page number is printed. The "&" signs are the printed ampersand (Et) in italic. "Sodomes" carries a small stray mark after "Sod" that I took as ornament. "bitumínis" is uncertain: the printed letters look like "bitumnis", so please check that word. "scelerata" is uncertain in its first letters, which look like a long s. Long s is written as plain s throughout. The catchword "Et" at the lower right is treated as a catchword, not a paragraph.
